verdict.rationale: Modal documents requesting GPUs programmatically through the `gpu` argument on Functions, via its Python SDK and CLI. It claims containers start in 1-2 seconds and that resources are available in seconds without quota requests, which meets the 'running code within minutes' part of the story. However, it is a serverless function and container model rather than a provisioned GPU instance, and there is no evidence of provisioning from the console. The API is SDK-based, and no OpenAPI spec was found. missing for 10: console-based GPU provisioning, a persistent on-demand instance lifecycle, independent hands-on corroboration of startup time.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: You can pick a specific GPU type for your Function via the `gpu` argument.
In contrast, _Modal spins containers_ up and down in 1-2 seconds.
Access the right resource for your workload in seconds without quota requests or long lead times.
The [Modal](https://modal.com/) Python SDK allows you to deploy high-performance serverless applications and programmatically interact with the Modal platform.
